subject: Unsteady estimate of the precision parameter of Besagproper2 model

messages.author: 4427b64dfcb5da5b
messages.subject: Unsteady estimate of the precision parameter of Besagproper2 model
parts:
I have some questions regarding unsteady estimates of the precision parameter of the Besagproper2 model.

Suppose I have a generalized Poisson regression model with a linear predictor composed of a single Besagproper2 CAR model proposed by Leroux et al:

Y ~ Pois(lambda)
Log(lambda) ~ eta
eta = phi ~ N(0, sigma^2Q^-1(W))
where Q(W) is a precision matrix defined in the Besagproper2 CAR model and sigma^2 is a variance parameter.

Then, I have two stages of simulations: (1) simulate the linear predictor eta itself and try to uncover the parameter lambda and precision in Q^-1; (2) simulate the Poisson integer Y based on the linear predictor and try to uncover the parameter lambda and precision in Q^-1. I have 10*10 areas and the Besagproper2 precision matrix Q is constructed.

The code follows:
(1) linear predictor simulation code:
simu_car <- inla.qsample(1, Q)      
formula <- y ~ 0  + f(sa, model = "besagproper2", graph = area.poly.adj, hyper=list(prec=list(prior='gaussian', param=c(prec, 0.01))))
 y <- simu_car
 modfit<- inla(formula,
                    data = data.frame(y, sa=1:100),
                    family = "gaussian", control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 10,fixed=TRUE))))

(2) Poisson simulation code:
simu_car <- inla.qsample(1, Q)
lambda <- exp(simu_car) (the same simu_car from the (1))
simu <- rpois(n = length(lambda), lambda = lambda)
formula <- y ~ 0  + f(sa, model = "besagproper2", graph = area.poly.adj, hyper=list(prec=list(prior='gaussian', param=c(prec, 0.01))))
 y <- simu
 modfit<- inla(formula,
                    data = data.frame(y, sa=1:100),
                    family = "poisson", E = rep(1, 100),
                    control.predictor = list(link = 1))

The question I am curious that is even if the same realization of eta (simu_car) is used in both the linear predictor and transformed to the realized integer to Poisson model to estimate the Besagproper2 parameter, the linear predictor simulation can uncover both the precision and lambda in a reasonable accuracy (not always, but most likely). However, the Poisson simulation model cannot. Sometimes the precision estimated from the Poisson simulation model is way too high (the magnitudes is too large) and the lambda parameter can be within a reasonable range.
I appreciate any thoughts on this. Thanks!

Thanks,
B

like

library(INLA)
inla.setOption(inla.mode="experimental")

let me know
H

If the model is flexible and data not that informative, you may add

r = inla(...)
r = inla.rerun(r)

but it shouldn't be needed really

messages.author: 4427b64dfcb5da5b
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Unsteady estimate of the precision parameter of Besagproper2 model
parts:
I found the problem lies in that I only have 100 observations that the Poisson model cannot converge while the linear predictor model can converge.

If I increase the number of observations to 10000, I can get reasonable estimates for the both Poisson model and the linear predictor model.


Thanks,
B
